newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended mixed to slightly higher on Wednesday in a thin market with most buying interest shown in maturities up to 2002.

Dealers said investors had been largely sidelined since Tuesday's news that eight of the 12 district banks in the U.S. Federal Reserve System had requested a hike in the discount rate triggered some nervousness in the market.
"The market is set for a 25 basis point rise," said one dealer, adding that a bigger increase could disrupt the market.
Dutch bonds followed fluctuating bund futures most of the day, with the sharply wider U.S. trade gap providing a slight positive impetus in the afternoon.
The U.S. trade gap widenend over 40 percent in July.
The widening of the yield gap between guilder bonds and bunds did not have any impact on the market. "Guilder bonds remain quite attractive to investors," said one dealer.
The January 2006 bond rose 0.07 to 99.77/85, with a bid yield of 6.02 or 14 basis points below the April 2006 bund versus minus 13 on Tuesday.
